solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A French litter-bearer, possibly old, [but] in good nick (9)

blocks.note: a dam is an animal mother, who bears a litter

annotation.surface: A French stretcher-bearer, perhaps elderly, who is nonetheless in fine shape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Litter-bearer' suggests someone carrying a stretcher; a litter is also a brood of puppies, so its bearer is the mother animal.
annotation.definitionFit: 'In good nick' is British slang for in good condition, which is what something unharmed is.

entries.clue: America finishes off peacekeeping force [in] practice (5)

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so the finishes of the next two words are their last letters

annotation.surface: The United States wrapping up an international peacekeeping mission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' reads as America ending the mission; here it takes the last letter of each of the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: usage is the customary way something is done, as in 'common usage'.

entries.clue: Outlaw does perhaps bother to case empty shop (9)

indicators.note: does are one example of deer, and 'perhaps' warns that the example stands for the wider class
to case something is to enclose it in a case, so DEER goes round SP
an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether a bandit bothers to scout an empty store before robbing it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb; it is the plural of doe, a female deer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a desperado is a reckless bandit, the outlaw of Wild West stories.

entries.clue: What may be used to blow up tiny figure? (9)

definitions.text: What may be used to blow up

blocks.clueFragment: What may be used to blow up

blocks.note: split the answer into two words: a very small person

annotation.surface: A riddle about what you would use to enlarge a small picture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' suggests enlarging a photo of a tiny figure; it means destroy. The tiny figure is a minute man, the answer read as two words.
annotation.definitionFit: The Minuteman is a US nuclear missile, built to blow things up; minute man is also literally a tiny person.

entries.clue: Rush to hold up craftsman[’s] glossy flyer (9,6)

indicators.note: to hold something up is to support it from below, and in a down entry BEETLE sits under GOLDSMITH

blocks.note: a goldsmith is a craftsman in gold
to beetle is to scurry or rush

annotation.surface: Someone hurrying to rob a jeweller's shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' suggests a robbery; in a down answer the word written underneath supports the one above, so the rush comes last.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the goldsmith beetle is a shiny metallic-green chafer, and like most beetles it can fly.

entries.clue: Cleaner of traps dishearteningly reassembled first of traps, not second (6,9)

indicators.note: something reassembled has been put back together in a new order
the first letter of traps, T, is used where the second letter, R, stood

blocks.note: the anagram fodder before the swap

annotation.surface: Someone clearing out animal traps, gloomily putting them back together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Traps' is slang for mouths, so a cleaner of traps cleans teeth. The setter uses the word twice on purpose: once in the definition, once to supply the swapped letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang sense: trap means mouth, as in 'shut your trap', and a dental hygienist cleans mouths.

entries.clue: What boozer, on reflection, has to accept? (5)

definitions.text: What boozer, on reflection, has to accept?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows a thing back to front, so BAR is turned round
to accept something is to take it in, so RAB takes EH inside it

blocks.note: a boozer is a pub, a BAR, turned round

annotation.surface: A question about what a heavy drinker must eventually come to terms with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' reads as the drinker, but in the wordplay it is British slang for a pub; the whole clue then describes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue asks what a drinker must accept after reflecting, and the answer is treatment for addiction.

entries.clue: Course note published charges (5)

indicators.note: to charge a gun or glass is to fill it, so RE is filled with OUT

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a book that is out has been published

annotation.surface: A report that the fees for a course of study have been announced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees; it is the verb, loading one piece into another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a course is the way taken from one place to another.

entries.clue: Mounted soldiers establish or secure borders (5)

indicators.note: a border is where two things meet, and the answer straddles the borders between the words

annotation.surface: Cavalry setting up or defending a frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' seems to be what the cavalry secure; it tells you the answer runs across word boundaries.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective sense: 'horse' means cavalry, as in 'a regiment of horse'.

entries.clue: Corporation’s shipping had finally departed behind schedule (9)

indicators.note: to ship cargo is to take it on board, so BELLY takes in ATE and D
the final part of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: corporation is jocular old slang for a paunch

annotation.surface: A company's shipments having left late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' suggests a business; old slang uses it for a pot belly.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverb for adverb swap: something done belatedly comes later than planned.

entries.clue: Team left behind close to tears in stadium (7)

indicators.note: to be left behind is to come after, so L goes at the end
the close of a word is where it ends, its last letter
'in stadium' puts S inside the word for stadium

annotation.surface: A team left weeping in its stadium after a defeat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left behind' reads as one phrase about the team; 'left' is just L and 'behind' places it last.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Arsenal is a London football club, one team of many.

entries.clue: University dons learnt about not taking sides (7)

indicators.note: to don clothing is to put it on, so the anagram wraps round U
'about' as in moved around, so the letters of learnt change places

annotation.surface: University dons who have found out about something, but stay impartial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dons' reads as university lecturers; it is the verb, to put on clothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a neutral party backs neither side in a dispute.

entries.clue: Something occurring twice revealed in letters from 1770s (5)

indicators.note: the answer shows up among the letters of the decade written out, and does so twice

blocks.note: write it out as seventeen-seventies; each word, minus its first S and its ending, gives the same five letters

annotation.surface: Something that happened twice in the historical record of the 1770s.
annotation.walkthrough: Write the decade in words, sEVENTeen sEVENTies, and the answer sits inside both halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an event is a thing that happens or occurs.

entries.clue: Government satisfied with introduction of new account (9)

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in, so N is brought inside MET

annotation.surface: A government pleased to bring in a new bank account.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Account' suggests banking; here it means a report or description.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a statement to police is an account of what happened.

entries.clue: Conservative receives millions [for] great opening (5)

annotation.surface: A Tory politician paid millions to open something grand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great opening' suggests a grand launch; it is a physical gap in the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a chasm is a deep, wide fissure, literally a great opening in the earth.

entries.clue: Knowledge and awareness essentially about noticing changes (9)

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so take the middle letter
the letters of noticing change their order

annotation.surface: A remark that knowledge and awareness mainly concern spotting changes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essentially about' reads as 'mostly concerning'; it is the middle letter of about.
annotation.definitionFit: A psychology term: cognition is the mental process of acquiring knowledge and awareness.

entries.clue: Popular man had to keep one part suppressed (9)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so HED holds I and BIT

annotation.surface: A well-liked man who had to hide one side of his personality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man had' becomes the contraction HE'D, with the apostrophe ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: inhibited feelings are held back, suppressed.

entries.clue: Performer[’s] short song encapsulating Ireland in verse (9)

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter
to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so BALLA surrounds ERIN

blocks.note: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

annotation.surface: A singer's brief ballad containing a verse about Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Performer' leads toward a singer, as the song suggests; the performer dances.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a ballerina is one kind of performer, a ballet dancer.

entries.clue: Name belonging to partner regularly seen [in] Finnish, we’re told (9)

definitions.note: the definition is 'finish', given by its sound-alike 'Finnish'

indicators.note: seen at regular intervals, so only every other letter shows

blocks.note: a term is a name for something
belonging to a club = in a club

annotation.surface: A Finnish word belonging to one's spouse, heard now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finnish, we're told' is the definition: said out loud it is 'finish'.
annotation.definitionFit: The word said is 'finish', and to terminate something is to bring it to an end.

entries.clue: Rodent chewed up house and border in garden (9)

indicators.note: the border of a garden is its edge, and the leading edge of the word is its first letter

blocks.note: ground = crushed small, as by teeth

annotation.surface: A rodent that has gnawed its way through a house and the flower bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chewed up' looks like the rodent's action; it is ground, crushed small.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the groundhog, or woodchuck, is a North American marmot, a rodent.

entries.clue: Vehicle[’s] choice of routes at T-junction close to motorway (5)

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, its last letter

blocks.note: at a T-junction you go left OR right: L OR R

annotation.surface: A driver choosing which way to turn at a junction near a motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: At a T-junction the only choices are left or right.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional use: lorry is the British word for a truck, a large goods vehicle.

entries.clue: Act as mediator keen on abandoning final decree out of hand (9)

indicators.note: abandoning its final letter, INTO is left as INT
a thing out of hand is out of control, so its letters run wild

blocks.note: INTO (keen on) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A mediator eager to scrap a final divorce decree that has got out of hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Final decree' looks like a legal term; 'final' belongs with 'abandoning' and cuts the end off INTO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to intercede is to step in between two parties on someone's behalf.

entries.clue: I’m grateful for every source that enlightens (5)

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thank you

annotation.surface: Thanks offered to every teacher or book that has educated us.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enlightens' suggests wisdom; here it means giving light.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a taper is a thin candle, and a candle literally lights up a room.

entries.clue: Jack[’s] hearing about gripping lives (5)

indicators.note: 'about' as in turned about, facing the other way
to grip something is to hold it inside your hand, so RAE holds IS

blocks.note: an ear is a hearing, as in 'give an ear', turned round

annotation.surface: A man named Jack at a court hearing on a matter of life and death.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the verb, as in jacking up a car.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: jacking up a car lifts it off the ground.

entries.clue: Cut off coverage for viewer hosted by network provider (5)

indicators.note: a host takes in a guest, so EE takes LID inside it

blocks.note: EE is a British mobile phone network

annotation.surface: A TV network cutting a programme's broadcast for viewers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coverage for viewer' suggests broadcasting; a viewer is an eye, covered by its lid.
annotation.definitionFit: A linguistic sense: to elide a sound or syllable is to cut it off or leave it out.

entries.clue: Put up resistance after introduction of extremely shocking treatment (5)

indicators.note: 'after' places R later in the answer than the letter before it
the introduction of a word is its opening, its first letter

blocks.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

annotation.surface: A patient fighting back against a very shocking therapy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up resistance' reads as one phrase; 'Put up' is the definition and resistance is just R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: builders erect or put up a wall, tent or statue.

entries.clue: Writer’s still [showing] sign of depression? (7)

blocks.note: the writer is 'I', so writer's = I'M
a still is a single photograph, a print

annotation.surface: An author who is still showing symptoms of low mood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood; here it is a dent pressed into a surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on depression: a physical dent leaves a mark pressed into a surface, like a footprint.

entries.clue: Copy India and China harnessing computing resources (7)

indicators.note: to harness something is to strap it in and use it, so MATE holds IT

blocks.note: I is India in the phonetic alphabet
china plate = mate in Cockney rhyming slang

annotation.surface: India and China copying each other in exploiting computer power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, a friend.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb for verb swap: to copy someone's manner or work is to imitate it.

entries.clue: Career set back by firm failing to complete tender (5)

indicators.note: something set back is moved backwards, so RUN is read in reverse
a word that fails to complete stops before its last letter

blocks.note: to career is to run headlong; RUN reversed
set = firm, as a jelly sets; SET without its last letter

annotation.surface: A career thrown off course by a company that could not finish a bid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Career' and 'tender' both look like business terms; career is the verb to rush, and tender means one who tends.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a tender is someone who tends, and a nurse is one who tends the sick.

entries.clue: Outgoing SMS by madman has first letter appearing last (9)

indicators.note: the opening letter, T, is taken from the front and moved to the end

blocks.note: an SMS is a text message
a raver is someone raving mad

annotation.surface: A text from a lunatic signed off in a strange order.
annotation.walkthrough: TEXT + RAVER gives TEXTRAVER; move its opening T to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective used as a noun: an extravert, usually spelt extrovert, is a sociable, outgoing person.
